subject: Lawful access handling and air‑gapped operational Q&A
messages:
From: Martin Cole <martin.cole@hightowerhealth.com>
To: camila.reyes@redwood.ai
Cc: security@hightowerhealth.com
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Hightower RFP: lawful access + air‑gapped ops Qs

Camila —

Thanks for taking this RFP. We're consolidating the final security appendix and need more detail on how Redwood handles lawful access and forensic evidence for private (air‑gapped / on‑prem) deployments. Key areas we need clarified:

1) If a government or law‑enforcement request arrives for data stored in an on‑prem private deployment, what is the standard operating procedure? Who at Redwood (if anyone) can access customer data in a private deployment?
2) For air‑gapped installations, what evidence can you provide to show chain‑of‑custody for model weights and patch artifacts during offline upgrades?
3) Do you provide an auditable log export (hashes/timestamps) that our SOC team can ingest? In what format?
4) Any constraints around export controls / controlled models when deployed on‑prem?

Attached: RFP_private_deploy_questionnaire.xlsx — the sections in red are the must‑have answers.

Can you respond by COB Thursday PST? We're targeting procurement review next week.

—Martin
Martin Cole
Security Lead, Hightower Health

Cc: avery.johnson@redwood.ai, dev.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 12:45:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Hightower RFP: lawful access + air‑gapped ops Qs

Martin —

Appreciate the clear ask. High‑level responses below; I'll attach a short Q&A PDF and an integration matrix that maps evidence artifacts to our logging/exports. We can follow up with a short call if you want a walkthrough.

Summary answers (short):
- Access to on‑prem customer data: Redwood does not have blanket access to customer data in air‑gapped/offline deployments. Any remote support we provide is via customer‑initiated remote sessions. Physical access is controlled by the customer or their chosen operator.
- Chain‑of‑custody for offline upgrades: we provide a chain_of_custody_template.csv and signed manifests for model and patch bundles. Each bundle includes SHA‑256 checksums, signing user ID, and a timestamped manifest.
- Audit log exports: yes — logs are exportable as gzipped JSONL or signed CSV with checkpoints (hashes). We also provide a summary SHA file for each export for integrity verification.
- Export controls: Redwood verifies model license and export classification during onboarding; we do not push controlled models to on‑prem without explicit customer authorization.

Attachments: redwood_airgap_qna_v1.pdf, kms_integration_matrix.xlsx

Next steps: I added Dev (dev.patel) and Avery (Avery Johnson, Head of Enterprise) to answer technical and commercial edge cases. If that works, we'll provide the manifest templates and SOC snapshot by EOD.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Senior Solutions Engineer — Private Deployments

From: dev.patel@redwood.ai <dev.patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Hightower RFP: lawful access + air‑gapped ops Qs

Martin / Camila —

Adding some technical specifics for your SOC team. Excerpts below are from our on‑prem operational runbook and manifest signing process.

-- Runbook excerpt (upgrade flow for air‑gapped node):
1) Customer operator creates an upgrade bundle (tar.gz) on an isolated admin host.
2) Bundle is signed locally using customer HSM (recommended) or customer KMS key reference; Redwood supports both PKCS#11 HSM signing and external key references.
3) A manifest.json (human‑readable + checksums) is produced and hashed (SHA‑256).
4) The operator copies the bundle + manifest to removable media and physically transports to the air‑gapped environment where the admin verifies the signature and applies the bundle.

-- Example manifest lines (sample only):
# filename,sha256,signer,ts
model-v2.bin,3b7f9e2c...,deploy-admin@htw,2026-11-29T02:10:12Z
patch-20261201.tar.gz,8a1d4b6f...,deploy-admin@htw,2026-12-01T18:22:03Z

We can provide a signed sample manifest and the matching verification script (python) as part of evidence.

On lawful access: for private/on‑prem we do not wire any backdoor. If a lawful request reaches Redwood for systems we do not host/manage, our default is to refer request to the customer and provide only metadata we are contractually permitted to share (e.g., support ticket IDs, timestamps for vendor‑initiated support sessions). We document any disclosure in a confidentiality log and can provide that as part of an audit trail when permitted.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 11:10:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Hightower RFP: lawful access + air‑gapped ops Qs

Thanks, Camila and Dev — this is helpful. A couple follow ups from our compliance team:

• Employee roles & physical access: please enumerate Redwood employees (roles only — we don't need PII) who would ever be in scope to sign manifests or perform verification during a supervised on‑site upgrade.
• Chain‑of‑custody attestation: we need a one‑page attestation (signed) that the manifest format and verification scripts are as described and will be supported for the life of the contract (minimum 24 months).
• Export control examples: can you confirm whether you have ever delivered models with EAR restrictions in an on‑prem install? If yes, what controls were used?

Also — the procurement team asked whether you can provide a SOC2 snapshot (most recent) and a short list of third‑party hardware vendors you commonly recommend for air‑gapped installs (network appliances, HSM vendors).

If you can get the attestation and a draft roles list by EOD today we can include it in the procurement packet.

—Martin
From: camila.reyes@redwood.ai <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>

Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, avery.johnson@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 13:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Hightower RFP: lawful access + air‑gapped ops Qs

Martin —

Attached: chain_of_custody_template.csv and a SOC2 snapshot (soc2-snapshot-2026-09.pdf). Quick answers inline:

• Roles: typical Redwood roles that may be involved (roles only): Solutions Engineer (Field), Principal SRE (on call for packaging support), Enterprise Install Lead (supervised onsite), Release Engineer (artifact signing advisory). We will provide a redacted roles list in the attestation.

• Attestation: Draft one‑page attestation attached via DocuSign link here: https://www.docusign.com/sign/EXAMPLE-ATTACHMENT — it includes a 24‑month support commitment for manifest/verification compatibility and a list of the exported artifact formats (tar.gz, .bin, .json manifest).

• Exported models: Redwood has not delivered EAR‑restricted models into customer on‑prem without a contract amendment. For customers with controlled models we require additional authorization and operate under a documented export control plan (technical review + signoff).

• Preferred hardware vendors (examples): Thales (HSM), YubiHSM for smaller footprints, Fortinet appliances for edge segmentation, and Supermicro BMCs with strict IPMI isolation. This is a non‑exhaustive list — we can provide procurement SKUs.

Attachments: chain_of_custody_template.csv, soc2-snapshot-2026-09.pdf

I'll add Lauren (Legal) to the thread to coordinate the attestation signature. Can we schedule a 30‑minute callslot tomorrow 10–11am PT to finalize?

Thanks —
